# Verification analysis: etcd-member-replacement-rhel9

Job: `2026-09-04__13-53-04`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Run a three-member etcd cluster across `node1`, `node2`, and `node3` holding
> application keys.
>
> The member on `node3` is permanently lost and its data cannot be recovered.
> Replace it with a working member on that same system so the cluster is back to

## Trial `etcd-member-replacement-rhel9__yEEiYVr`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task contract are directly and coherently satisfied: a healthy 3-member etcd cluster was stood up and seeded with application keys, node3's member was realistically simulated as permanently lost (stopped, disabled, data wiped) while quorum on node1+node2 kept serving the keys, and the dead member was removed and replaced with a new working member on the same node3 host via a standard member remove/add + existing-cluster-state join, restoring a fully healthy 3/3 cluster with the original keys verified intact from multiple endpoints. Independently, the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was executed on all three nodes with complete, cross-verified evidence: pre-restart boot IDs and healthy baselines, reboot acknowledgements, distinct post-restart boot IDs, and full recovery of etcd, cluster health, membership, and data on each node — matching the fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots exactly.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.930 | 44/4 (+12 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Deploy a working three-member etcd cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
  - **Why:** etcd v3.5.17 installed and started on all three nodes with a shared initial-cluster config; endpoint health and member list confirm all three members healthy/started, and four application keys under /app/config and /app/service were written and read back successfully.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-37de731eb9fc4e71`, `cmd-2f43c1b71ba14dc3`, `cmd-21206ff4a2a34e54`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Simulate permanent, unrecoverable loss of the node3 member
  - **Why:** A healthy baseline was captured on node3's own endpoint before disruption, then etcd was stopped, disabled, and its data directory deleted on node3, directly representing an unrecoverable member loss.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-97f69fffe0c24419`, `cmd-2764bcdcb2ae49ed`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Cluster (via remaining quorum) stays available/serves keys during the node3 outage
  - **Why:** With node3 down, node1+node2 (2/3 quorum) were directly observed as healthy, listing all members and serving the full original key set, demonstrating the bounded-disruption behavior expected of a quorum-preserving replacement.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-491a27b19912446f`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** Replace the dead node3 member with a new, working member on the same node3 host
  - **Why:** The dead member ID was removed via `member remove` from the surviving quorum, a new member was added via `member add` with node3's peer URL, and etcd was reconfigured with ETCD_INITIAL_CLUSTER_STATE=existing and started successfully on node3, joining as the new member.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1a012c398e314727`, `cmd-e62bbb0092ae46d0`, `cmd-a9abbb7ea2b54372`
- **R5 — Satisfied:** Cluster restored to three healthy members with existing application keys intact
  - **Why:** Post-replacement endpoint health shows all three endpoints healthy, member list shows all three members started (node3 with new member ID), and both node1 and node3's own endpoint return the complete, unmodified original key set.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-11ac92cfd7864c87`, `cmd-6a64862ff44d43ba`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Reviewed the full chronological command trace: every state-changing action (binary installs, firewall port openings, systemd unit/config creation, cluster bootstrap, the node3 stop/wipe used to simulate loss, member remove/add, and the three sequential mandatory reboots) maps directly to a required setup step, the requested disruption/replacement scenario, or the independent restart-evidence protocol. No troubleshooting experiments, abandoned services, or unrelated mutations were found; after-executor snapshots show zero failed services and clean package-manager state on all nodes. The only residue is downloaded/extracted etcd install artifacts (etcd.tar.gz, etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64/) left in /tmp on all three nodes — a minor, low-risk, non-destructive leftover from a necessary installation step that was never cleaned up.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-b555aff2db814a09`, `cmd-2764bcdcb2ae49ed`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`
